_comment: The missions (SPEC.md §12 M27, ROADMAP.md Phase 2): the game is an engine plus a mission. Each entry is printed on the contents page, in this order. `status` is `playable`, `draft` or `coming`; a coming mission is printed but stamped NEXT YEAR'S ANNUAL and cannot be chosen, so it needs only `id`, `title`, `place`, `page` and `blurb`. A draft one (M28) is printed and stamped as a coming one, but `?mission=<id>` plays it, so it can be tried on the live site before it is announced; it needs everything a playable one does. A playable one names its `map` and `roster` files, and a `rules` and `enemies` patch deep-merged over data/rules.json and data/enemies.json before the difficulty's (the same merge difficulty.json uses; a key must already exist, except a new objective kind under `objectives` or a new enemy type under `types`). `win` is one of the fixed win conditions in src/missions.js, never a code branch for one mission. `briefing` opens the orders; `tagline` runs along the foot of the title card; `levels` (M28, optional) is the mission's own part of each difficulty level, keyed by the level's id in data/difficulty.json: a `rules` and `enemies` patch merged after the level's own, and a `summary` printed before the level's; what a level does to this mission's targets lives here, what it does in every mission lives in difficulty.json. `words` are the mission's own phrases the rules' text needs (the cut line's, the RAF diversion's card and log line); `dialogue` (M28) replaces any of the men's lines for this mission, keyed by his roster id, over the roster file's; `titleCard` is its painted title card (ART-ASSETS.md §7); `portraits` (M29b, optional) is a folder of the mission's own portraits, named as in assets/portraits, each tried before the usual one; `endSounds` are the sound.js cues for the back page. `?mission=<id>` in the address picks one, and `default` is the one when none is asked for.

missions.title: The Rail Bridge
missions.blurb: Six men drop by night to blow the bridge that carries the line to the coast, and must be out before dawn.
missions.tagline: SIX MEN · ONE BRIDGE · DAWN AT TWENTY
missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop behind enemy lines.

hard.summary: Blowing a target calls up reinforcements to guard the way out: two squads for the Rail Bridge, one for the Fuel Dump, none once the Telephone Exchange is down.

missions.title: The Airfield
missions.blurb: Aircraft in their pens on an Axis landing ground, one charge each. Every one more is greed against the dawn.
missions.tagline: SIX MEN · EIGHT AIRCRAFT · DAWN AT TWENTY
missions._rules: SPEC.md §13. Lewes bombs are small, so the scouts carry one each as well as the sappers (M29b, the operator's: with none, and two a sapper, the scouts had nothing to do here); still five in the stick with Nunn's. The win pays 10 on top of each aircraft's own 2, since no target here is worth the bridge's 10 on its own. Three new objective kinds; their numbers are Normal's, first guesses for M30's balance.
missions._enemies: The perimeter car (SPEC.md §13): fast, so it reaches a noise first; it can be suppressed but never killed or knifed.

hard.summary: Six aircraft are wanted: with five bombs, the bowser has to go.

missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop on an enemy landing ground.

words.lineIsDown: the field telephones are already down

missions.title: The Aqueduct
missions.blurb: A great aqueduct in the mountains that wants every charge you carry, and a boat on the coast that will not wait.
